papers.title: A Comprehensive Analysis of Fermi Gamma-Ray Burst Data. IV. Spectral Lag and its Relation to Ep Evolution
papers.classification: sample-member with FULL time-resolved spectroscopy - the strongest external frame for this burst and the NEWEST (Phase 3b: read and diff this one first)
papers.frame: brightest-NaI TTE (smallest source angle); gtBurst + HEASOFT 6.20; RMFIT 4.3.2; BAND function; bins at SNR>40; chi2_r reported. Component coverage = the single pulse, [-0.83,+16.30] s (~18% of the T90 span).
verbatim_anchors: Table 3 p.51 (layout-verified by word coordinates, two-column table): 'bn110605183 (-0.5-25.0)' with band (2) 0.85 +/- 0.49, band (3) 1.73 +/- 0.41, band (5) 2.48 +/- 0.41

definitions_copied_with_the_numbers_T3.Ep: nu-F-nu peak of the Band function; alpha/beta are photon indices, negative sign convention
definitions_copied_with_the_numbers_T3.lag_tau_hat: CCF lag measured WITH RESPECT TO the 8-25 keV band, MC-Gaussian errors; bands (1) 25-50, (2) 50-100, (3) 100-300, (4) 300-1000 keV NaI, (5) 300-1000 keV BGO, (6) 1000-5000 keV BGO. tau_hat RISES with energy here => POSITIVE lag = soft photons arrive later
definitions_copied_with_the_numbers_T3.tau_hat_31: lag between 100-300 and 25-50 keV (the older literature's convention)
definitions_copied_with_the_numbers_T3.W: FWHM of the pulse observed in 8 keV - 1 MeV (their Sect. 3.2). WARNING: the SAME symbol W is defined in their Sect. 3.1 as W = T_d + T_r at the 10% level - one paper, one symbol, two definitions (trap T3, the Lu+2018 specimen already recorded in the skill)
definitions_copied_with_the_numbers_T3.kE: slope of log Ep = kE*log(t+t0) + b; class H requires kE < -0.2; our burst kE = -0.77 +/- 0.14, near the sample centre (-0.8)
definitions_copied_with_the_numbers_T3.k_tau_hat: slope of tau_hat = k_tau_hat * log E + b
definitions_copied_with_the_numbers_T3.Evolution H: hard-to-soft (H2S), and their Sect. 3.1 states the classification is made BY EYE - a judgement, not a fit
definitions_copied_with_the_numbers_T3.pulse_t0: NOT a free parameter: fixed at the time of 0.1*Im on the RISE, then r and d fitted; r and d are DEGENERATE with t0 and are only comparable to a fit adopting the same rule

papers.prompt_sections: READ: Sect. 2 (sample + data reduction: brightest-NaI rule, RMFIT/Band, SNR>40 binning, Eq. 1 Kocevski pulse, lag bands and the 8-25 keV reference) and Sect. 3.1-3.2 (H2S vs tracking classification, kE, k_tau_hat, W); plus our four rows in Tables 1-4. ALL PROMPT - this paper has no afterglow content. DEFER: Sect. 4 (phenomenological curvature-effect simulation) unless the HLE thread reopens.

papers.title: A New Measurement of the Spectral Lag of Gamma-Ray Bursts and its Implications for Spectral Evolution Behaviors
papers.classification: sample-member (1 of 50 bright single-pulse GBM bursts); independent lag/pulse-width measurement in a DIFFERENT formalism from Lu+2018
papers.frame: TTE rebinned into NINE log-spaced energy channels; per-channel polynomial background + GAUSSIAN pulse (IDL GAUSSFIT); PyMultiNest on t_peak(E) = t0 + tau*(E/1keV)^-beta and delta(E) = omega*(E/1keV)^-gamma. NaI used = n2 (our brightest detector). Binsize 1.00 s.

definitions_copied_with_the_numbers_T3.T90: ADOPTED from the GBM catalog, 50-300 keV - not an independent measurement (T6 chain: their Sect. 2 names Gruber+2014 and von Kienlin+2014 as the source; the value is byte-identical to our bcat)
definitions_copied_with_the_numbers_T3.binsize: nominally 5% of T90 (= 4.13 s here) but 'modified manually to keep them close to 5% of the genuine pulse width' -> they used 1.00 s, i.e. they judged the genuine pulse ~20 s wide, not 83 s. Independent corroboration of the T50-based core.
definitions_copied_with_the_numbers_T3.t0: t_peak(E -> infinity), the limiting arrival time of the most energetic photons
definitions_copied_with_the_numbers_T3.tau: the LIMITING SPECTRAL LAG AT 1 keV = t_peak(1 keV) - t_peak(infinity). NOT a CCF lag and NOT comparable to Lu's tau_hat_31. Sample median 12.6 s; our burst 25.4 s = a long-lag object.
definitions_copied_with_the_numbers_T3.omega: limiting RMS Gaussian HALF-width at 1 keV (sample median 5.2 s; ours 16.3 s)
definitions_copied_with_the_numbers_T3.gamma: index of delta(E) = omega*E^-gamma (sample median 0.21; ours 0.310). They read gamma~0.5 as synchrotron cooling and gamma~0.25 as SSC/curvature/Doppler - ours sits between.
definitions_copied_with_the_numbers_T3.delta_t_HR: CCF delay between the HARDNESS-RATIO curve and the TOTAL light curve (their Sect. 5) - a hardness-INTENSITY delay, a different physical quantity from any photon lag; never diff it against tau_hat

papers.prompt_sections: READ: Sect. 2 (nine-channel construction, Gaussian-pulse selection - note the burst had to be pinpointable in ALL nine channels, so its single-pulse status is externally corroborated), Sect. 3 (Eqs. 2 and 5, the t0/tau/beta/omega/gamma meanings), Sect. 5 (delta_t_HR and the HIT-vs-HTS hardness discussion), and our Table 1 row. ALL PROMPT. DEFER: Sects. 6-7 (pulsar/dispersion analogies, population correlations).

frame_alignment_for_P3.component_coverage_T9: ONE emission complex, no precursor, no separate episode; T90START = +1.536 s so there is NO pre-trigger emission (this burst is NOT a D4 case). But the frames cover different FRACTIONS of it: our stamped window [-1.548,+30.618] s ~ 36% of the T90 span (and contains ALL of T50 [4.86,28.93]); catalog flnc [-2.048,+60.416] ~ 75%; bcat T90 [1.54,84.23] = 100%; Lu+2018 [-0.83,+16.30] ~ 18%; Shao+2017 effective (-0.5,25.0) ~ 29%.
frame_alignment_for_P3.consequence: Ep evolves monotonically hard-to-soft (327 -> 186 -> 152 -> 103 keV, Lu+2018), so a LONGER interval is necessarily SOFTER. Any Ep the catalog reports over [-2.048,+60.416] s MUST come out below ours over [-1.548,+30.618] s. That is a frame difference, never a discrepancy. Ordered ladder: Lu bin1 327 keV > pflx 216/231 > Lu bin2 186 > flnc Band/Comp 151/186 > Lu bin4 103.
frame_alignment_for_P3.detector_sets: OUR approved set = n2, n5, b0 (Vikas Chand, human_gui, 2026-07-19T22:18:36Z). GBM SPECTRAL catalog set = BGO_00, NAI_02, NAI_05 = IDENTICAL. frame_alignment_for_P3.multi_instrument_consensus_Rossi2026: NOT APPLICABLE in the usual sense: Konus-Wind, INTEGRAL SPI-ACS, Suzaku-WAM and Mars Odyssey all DETECTED this burst (von Kienlin+2014 'Mo, K, IA, W') but NONE published a spectrum for it (checked by ADS four-form + 6 supplementary forms + a targeted Konus web query). There is no inter-instrument spread to fold into the error. The only spread available is between analyses of the SAME GBM data over DIFFERENT intervals, which is a frame effect and must not be inflated into a systematic.
frame_alignment_for_P3.Ep_conventions: Band Ep and Comp Ep are both nu-F-nu peak energies (rmfit parametrisation); Ep(Comp) > Ep(Band) is curvature, not units. SBPL Ebreak = 96.81 keV is a BREAK energy and is NOT an Ep - never diff it against one (L21).

finding: GRB 110605A has NO dedicated-analysis paper and NO circulars. Its entire refereed footprint is three papers, and NONE of them fits a physical model to it: Lu+2018 (time-resolved Band + Kocevski pulse + CCF lags, the newest and strongest frame), Shao+2017 (nine-channel Gaussian lag formalism), Hurley+2017 (an IPN detection row we could not extract because the publisher blocks bots and no eprint exists). No redshift, no afterglow, no host, no SN, no photospheric or synchrotron claim, no BB claim, no two-break claim - by anyone, ever. Two independent teams did nevertheless certify what our Stage 1 assumed: the burst is a clean SINGLE PULSE (Shao required a Gaussian to pinpoint it in all nine energy channels; Lu fit one Kocevski pulse at chi2_r = 1.14), its Ep evolution is HARD-TO-SOFT (Lu class 'H', kE = -0.77 +/- 0.14, Ep 327 -> 103 keV), and its brightest detector is n2 - the detector our human-approved Stage 1 also chose, alongside n5 and b0, which is EXACTLY the GBM spectral catalog's own set. Because nobody has ever proposed a spectral component beyond Band/CPL/SBPL for this burst, whatever our union rule and DSBPL do here is an UNPUBLISHED DECISION to be scored against the expert band, not a literature reconciliation. That makes this burst unusually clean evidence in the AI-Scientist program: there is no published answer to memorize.
